seen.cipher: Regest 145344: 'Andreas Gembicki ... – Zrínyi Péter gróf (orig. latin, mellékelve hozzá titkosíráskulcs is, legalább három különböző)': the letter is described as Latin original, with cipher keys (at least three different ones) enclosed; no ciphertext is mentioned. vetting.key_check: The item is itself key material: at least three cipher keys enclosed with Gembicki's letter (fol. 75-83; Lang: key at f. 77). Worth a DECODE key-record entry (decode_updates/queue.json) with this metadata.

vetting.closed: Gembicki's letter of 4 Oct 1669 to Péter Zrínyi is a Latin original with cipher keys enclosed, not a ciphertext; it is key material for DECODE, not an open cipher.

2688.note: All four regests the row names say the cipher is deciphered on file (two interlinear, two on a separate sheet) and all four are printed in Károlyi, Fráter György levelezése, Történelmi Tár 1878. Record errors: 154594 (29 May 1542, Déva) is to Johann Wese, archbishop of Lund, not of Esztergom, and the four pieces sit at fol. 193-196, 205-207, 210-215 and 218.

seen.extent: Four letters of Frater Georgius (Martinuzzi) of 29 May, 17 Sep, 6 Oct and 12 Oct 1542; the ciphered share is not stated.

vetting.key_check: Each piece carries its own contemporary decipherment (interlinear or separate sheet), which gives the 1542 key; catalogue 885 / targets/ibrahim1548 hold a later Martinuzzi key. Not compared here because nothing is left to read.
vetting.duplicates: known.py on shelfmark and names: catalogue 503 and 885 are other years; no duplicate row for these four letters.
vetting.closed: All four 1542 Martinuzzi letters carry a contemporary decipherment on file and are printed in Károlyi, Történelmi Tár 1878, so nothing is left unread.

2787.note: Not assessed to a verdict. TNA's description (C12835255) gives ff. 316-321 as a 'Letter (in code)' of 15 May 1799 and ff. 306-313 as Osborn forwarding 'extracts of a letter (which is in code)' of Rainier; it does not say whether the extracts are the coded text or a decoding, whether 'code' is a cipher or a naval signal code, nor what the two East India House papers (ff. 314-315) are. 2878.note: Not assessed to a verdict. The OAC guide (read by curl 16 Nov 2026) gives only a folder title 'Ciphers' (Box 1, Folder 1, identifier 156369) and the collection note 'Ciphers, letters, official patents, documents ... collected by Montauti while special envoy' (Tuscan envoy at Vienna 1670-1723); nothing says whether these are cipher keys (most likely for an envoy's own papers, which would make them key material for his Mediceo despatches) or enciphered letters.
